value.why: tail -1/-2 clips the 'X% tests passed' verdict line, making green runs unreadable as pass/fail; use tail -5 or grep 'tests passed'. REPAIRED 2026-08-03: the old pattern was 'ctest[^|]*\|\s*tail\s+-(n\s*)?[12]\b' and could never fire — rabadon matches each rule against a PARSED SEGMENT surface and a '|' is the segment boundary, so no surface ever contains one (measured: gate exit 0 on 'ctest --test
new_flats, benchmark-58, dataset, engine/dist and patterns_real are copyrighted never-push sources (CLAUDE.md GİZLİLİK); explicitly adding them to the index must be blocked before it happens.

ctest -N / --show-only only LISTS tests and runs nothing; its exit code is 0 whatever the suite does, so it is never a pass/fail signal — run the real suite. REPAIRED 2026-08-03: the old pattern was 'ctest\s+-N\b.*grep\s+-c' and could never fire, because it needed the pipe and the parsed surface splits on it (measured: gate exit 0 on 'ctest -N | grep -c Test'). The dry run is now refused on its ow
Repo holds untracked unignored dirs (Logs/, patterns_real additions) that must never be staged wholesale, and other Claude sessions write in this tree; explicit-path git add stays allowed.
macOS has no `timeout` binary; the command dies before the real work runs — use gtimeout or drop it.
`echo exit=$?` after a pipe reports the last pipe stage's status, not the command under test, so a RED suite reads as exit=0.
macOS has no `timeout` binary; the command dies before the real work runs — use gtimeout or drop it.
Reverse-applying an old commit onto HEAD silently no-ops when the file has drifted, making a regression test look passing; use a worktree at the parent commit instead.
In-place perl/sed rewrites of tracked .rs files silently mutate logic outside the editor's tracking and produce phantom test failures.
Copying a scratch .rs over a tracked source file bypasses Edit/Write and the cargo fmt step, which is what broke the fmt gate here.
In-place scripted rewrites of engine source and its test expectations edit both sides blind and let the two drift into contradicting each other.
Discarding stderr from the test runner turns a diagnosable failure into a bare test name and forces a second full run.

value.why: the post-run hook reported tests are RED twice tonight while make test exited 0 with 0 failed, because the net verdict in .rabadon/net.json persists and nothing invalidates it when a later run goes green. the gate diagnosed its own false signal both times

its own message says it fires once per session and it fired three times, because the driftChallenged flag lives in one state file capped at the last 4 sessions while 7 were running. the rule is right, the session model under it is not

its dot-h alternative carries no boundary so it also matches dot-html and dot-hpp. it refused a line whose only offence was carrying an in-place editor example as quoted DATA, and then it refused this very report for the same reason. fix is a negative lookahead after the h

2>&1 is a file-descriptor duplication, not a write to a file named 1; it refused four of five agent sessions on their first or second command. fixed in 8c9625b, native/fd_dup_test.sh holds both directions
